standing.title: Smorgasburg Prospect Park
standing.address: Breeze Hill, Prospect Park (enter at Lincoln Road), Brooklyn, NY
standing.description: Brooklyn's open-air food market at Breeze Hill in Prospect Park, with dozens of independent vendors. Free to enter; pay per stall.
standing.time_note: Sundays 11am-6pm; arrive before noon to beat the line.
standing.practical_note: Entirely outdoors; check the forecast and bring water in heat.
standing.date_idea_reason: Open-air food market you can graze through together, then walk into Prospect Park.
standing.why_now: Runs every Sunday of the season and pairs naturally with a Prospect Park afternoon.

standing.title: NYC Resistor Public Craft Night
standing.description: Open craft night at the NYC Resistor hacker collective: bring a project, use the space, meet members. Free and open to the public, 18 and over.
standing.time_note: Mondays and Thursdays 6:30-9:30pm. Free, but 18+ only.
standing.practical_note: Fourth-floor walkup; confirm on Eventbrite since craft night is occasionally cancelled for private classes.
standing.date_idea_reason: A free, hands-on makerspace evening is an unusual low-cost date with something to actually do.
standing.why_now: Runs twice a week year-round and is one of the few genuinely free weeknight drop-in activities.

standing.title: Whitney Museum free Friday evening
standing.description: The Whitney is free to all every Friday evening from 5 to 10pm, and also on the second Sunday of each month.
standing.time_note: Free admission Fridays 5-10pm. Free tickets are limited and released in advance.
standing.practical_note: Reserve the free timed ticket ahead; walk-up availability runs out on busy evenings.
standing.date_idea_reason: Free evening museum hours next to the High Line and a dense stretch of bars, so the museum is the anchor rather than the whole plan.
standing.why_now: A standing free window that makes a good anchor for a Friday evening in the Meatpacking District.

standing.title: Queens Night Market
standing.address: Behind the New York Hall of Science, 47-01 111th St, Flushing Meadows Corona Park, Queens, NY 11368
standing.description: Open-air night market behind the New York Hall of Science with about a hundred independent food, art, and merchandise vendors, deliberately kept low-priced.
standing.time_note: Saturdays 4pm to midnight. Note the seasonal gap between late August and mid September.
standing.practical_note: Outdoors and cash-friendly; the adjacent lot charges for parking, so the 7 train is easier.

price.display: Free entry; most dishes capped at a few dollars

standing.date_idea_reason: Cheap, walkable, and genuinely varied: dozens of cuisines in one loop, good for a low-pressure evening.
standing.why_now: Runs every Saturday evening in season; the 7 train to 111th St drops you four blocks away.

standing.title: MoMA free Friday evening
standing.description: MoMA offers free admission on Friday evenings. Free tickets are limited, released in advance, and go quickly.
standing.time_note: Free Friday evenings, roughly 4-8pm. Confirm the current window and ticket release on moma.org.
standing.practical_note: Book the free timed ticket the moment it is released; the line for walk-ups is long.
standing.why_now: A standing weekly free window at a museum that is otherwise one of the most expensive in the city.

holiday_plan.intro: For Oct. 10-12, prioritize timed/reserved art destinations and rail-friendly Hudson Valley plans; for car trips, keep the destination within the three-hour normal-drive radius but verify same-day traffic before committing.

trips.title: CAR-FREE: Beacon for Dia Beacon, river walk, and a Saturday music/art program
trips.why: Dia Beacon is open Friday-Monday, 10 am-5 pm, with arrival before 4:30 pm; Oct. 10 has Saturday Studio and the Isang Yun: Images concert tied to Haegue Yang: Through, and Renée Green: The Equator Has Moved is listed through Oct. 12.
trips.transport: CAR-FREE: Metro-North Hudson Line to Beacon; Dia says it is an 8-10 minute walk from Beacon station and trains run hourly during museum operating hours. CAR-OPTIONAL: Dia lists the drive from NYC at approximately 80 minutes in normal conditions.
trips.time_budget: Easy full day; allow museum time plus Main Street or waterfront time.
trips.booking_note: Advance Dia reservations are suggested but not required; the Oct. 10 concert is free with museum admission but has limited seating/registration, and Saturday Studio registration opens Oct. 2 at 9 am. If driving, Dia notes limited onsite parking and possible holiday/weekend overflow to Beacon station.

trips.title: CAR-FREE: Cold Spring foundry history, river village, and short nature walks
trips.why: West Point Foundry Preserve is an outdoor industrial-history site listed as free and open year-round from dawn to dusk; the Putnam History Museum is a useful add-on on Saturday or Sunday, while Monday is better kept outdoors because the museum is closed Mondays.
trips.transport: CAR-FREE: Metro-North Hudson Line to Cold Spring; the MTA station page is official for timetable lookup. CAR-OPTIONAL: drive if pairing with Bear Mountain or additional Hudson Highlands stops.
trips.time_budget: Easy-to-moderate day trip; keep plans flexible if adding hikes because daylight and trail conditions matter.
trips.booking_note: No timed entry for West Point Foundry Preserve found; verify any village alerts, trail closures, and individual shop or museum holiday hours before going.

trips.title: CAR-FREE OR CAR-OPTIONAL: Storm King sculpture landscape day
trips.why: Storm King is a distinctive outdoor art day in peak fall season; official pages list Wednesday-Monday operation, October weekend early opening, museum/store/cafe information, and October tickets available.
trips.transport: CAR-FREE: Coach USA offers a Port Authority-to-Storm King round-trip package that includes transportation and museum admission. CAR-OPTIONAL: drive to onsite parking, or take Metro-North to Beacon plus a car/taxi connection; Storm King says Beacon station is about 30 minutes away by car.
trips.time_budget: Full day; the site is large and transit connections need padding.
trips.booking_note: Pre-purchased tickets are essential to guarantee admission and parking; onsite tickets may be limited or unavailable for some time slots. Confirm whether the Coach USA package has seats for the exact date before relying on it.

trips.title: CAR-REQUIRED OR AMTRAK-PLUS-CAR: Hudson and Olana one-night art/nature escape
trips.destination: Hudson and Olana State Historic Site, NY
trips.why: Olana’s landscape is free and open daily 8 am-sunset, and its 2026 individual-tour page explicitly says tours are open Monday, Oct. 12; pairing Olana with Hudson makes the longer trip practical as a one-night escape.
trips.transport: CAR-REQUIRED for the simplest NYC-to-Olana weekend and local movement. Amtrak to Hudson may be a car-free component, but Amtrak official pages returned 403 here, so schedules and station details remain unconfirmed in this research.
trips.time_budget: One night recommended; doable as a long day only if driving conditions and tour timing line up.
trips.booking_note: Olana says tours sell out quickly and advanced reservations are strongly recommended; verify exact tour inventory before booking lodging. If relying on rail, confirm Amtrak schedules directly because the official Amtrak page was blocked.

trips.title: CAR-FREE WITH SHORT RIDE OR CAR-OPTIONAL: Planting Fields Gold Coast gardens
trips.why: Planting Fields offers a 400-acre former Gold Coast estate with gardens, greenhouses, nature walks, and seasonal Coe Hall tours; it is a lower-lift Long Island nature/culture alternative to Hudson Valley foliage routes.
trips.transport: CAR-FREE: LIRR to Oyster Bay, then a short local taxi/rideshare to Planting Fields; MTA station and schedule pages are official. CAR-OPTIONAL: drive directly to the state historic park.
trips.time_budget: Half-to-full day depending on Coe Hall tour availability and garden time.
trips.booking_note: The New York State Parks page points visitors to Planting Fields for details; the Planting Fields page loaded only limited text here, so verify hours, Coe Hall tour times, and any holiday programming directly before going.

local_ideas.title: Dia Chelsea: public tour of David Lamelas: The Machine
local_ideas.why: A low-friction city option: Dia Chelsea is free, open Wednesday-Saturday 12-6 pm, and lists a public tour on Saturday, Oct. 10 at 1 pm; reservations are suggested but not required.

local_ideas.title: NYBG Fall-O-Ween in the Bronx
local_ideas.why: NYBG’s official Fall-O-Ween page describes pumpkins, gourds, fall flowers, seasonal activities, special weekends, and select-night light trail programming; exact date-by-date availability for Oct. 10-12 should be verified on the admission/calendar flow before going.

local_ideas.title: Central Park Conservancy official tour or self-guided foliage walk
local_ideas.why: A no-travel-fuss long-weekend fallback with official Conservancy tours available through its tour page; choose only a listed bookable slot, or use it as a self-guided park day if the tour calendar does not fit.

checks: Verify exact Oct. 10-12 transit schedules close to departure; holiday service patterns can differ from ordinary weekdays/weekends.
For every timed museum, garden, bus package, tour, or concert, confirm date-specific availability before building the day around it; this research did not check inventory or purchase tickets.
For car-required trips, re-check normal and live traffic before departure; the three-hour radius does not guarantee long-weekend drive times.
For outdoor plans, check weather, trail/park alerts, daylight, and any site-specific closures or air-quality changes.
If using blocked sources such as Amtrak, Smithsonian/NMAI, or Met pages, verify directly in a browser because fetched access was blocked or rate-limited here.
